newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says Q1 vehicle deliveries up 9.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: VW says Q1 vehicle deliveries up 9.5 pct.

text.p: Volkswagen AG said on Thursday that group customer deliveries rose 9.5 percent in the first three months of 1997, spurred by double-digit growth in foreign markets but marred by slow growth in western Europe.

VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech said in the text of a speech at the German carmaker's annual news conference that VW saw an increase of 27.9 percent in deliveries of vehicles to customers in eastern Europe and a 15.2 percent gain in North America over 1996 first quarter levels..
But deliveries in western Europe, the German carmaker's largest market, rose a mere 2.5 percent, VW said.
Among other regions of the world, VW said sales in Latin America and Africa rose 17.9 percent and Asia-Pacific sales rose 26.5 percent.
